title: Cinder Logistics - Warmup Walkthrough and Loadshape Playbook
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the field experiments we ran for Cinder Logistics during the Aug 2029 POC sprint. Goal: find consistent, repeatable warmup and loadshape strategies to keep p95 latency under 240ms for a 256-token average generation while minimizing incremental GPU-hours and token cost. Deliverables here: what we tested, raw observations, a simple cost model, and concrete recommendations for the customer demo and production rollout.

Key takeaways (short):
- KV-cache priming with a 10% synthetic prefix sweep reduces cold-start p95 by ~45% and steady-state p95 by ~8% for their mixed small/medium prompts.
- A lightweight connection warmup (50 parallel gRPC streams per pool node for 30s) fixes the ~150ms connection tail observed on first traffic burst.
- Adaptive microbatching (target latency 160ms) produced 12–18% cost savings vs fixed batch size while keeping p95 SLA.
- Recommend a combined strategy for the demo: cache priming + connection warmup + adaptive batch policy.

Hardware and runtime configuration used:
- Cluster: Redwood Dedicated, 4 x A800 (80GB) GPUs per node, 6 nodes in pool (24 GPUs total) with 1 spare for warmfailover.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v4.12.3 (attention kernels: fused-rotary, qkv-fusion), quantization profile: dynamic-8-bit (activations float16).
- Model used: open-cinder-7b-instruct (sharded, KV-compatible snapshot), typical generation length: 40–256 tokens, average 96 tokens for our synthetic mix.

Traffic profiles tested (why these were chosen):
1) Demo steady: 200 qps sustained for 5 minutes (simulate demo slide barrage).
2) Microbursts: 2s spikes to 1200 qps, repeating every 90s (customer saw this pattern during order surges).
3) Warmstart ramp: cold start then ramp 0 -> 300 qps over 45s (to reproduce first-login spike).
4) Mixed tail: mixture of small (10–30 token) rerank requests (60%) and medium (80–160 token) summarizations (40%).

Experiments and observations:
A) Baseline (no priming, fixed batch size 32):
- Demo steady p50/p95/p99: 68ms / 312ms / 610ms.
- Microbursts: p95 jumped to 520ms on first spike; connection resets observed in 6/30 runs.
- Cost estimate: $0.058 per 1k tokens (baseline token egress + GPU amortized) for this profile.

B) KV-cache priming (full prefix sweep + synthetic fallbacks):
- Method: run a short suite of 100 representative prefixes that cover 80% of the customers' prompt entry points; write cache snapshot to S3 and load into each node at startup.
- Results: demo steady p95 down to 176ms; p99 reduced to 420ms. Substantial improvement on medium-length prompts.
- Cold-start benefit: first-request p95 reduced by ~360ms on average.

C) Connection warmup and gRPC tuning:
- Method: after node spin-up, issue 50 concurrent keepalive/gRPC streams for 30s to preinitialize TLS handshakes and session caches. Also set keepalive interval to 30s for demo nodes.
- Results: eliminated the consistent ~120–180ms first-connection penalty seen in baseline microbursts; reduced occurrence of transient connection failures to 0/30 runs.

D) Adaptive microbatching policy (latency-constrained optimizer):
- Method: runtime observes token-per-request distribution and dynamically adjusts batch size so the estimated completion time stays below target 160ms; max batch cap 64.
- Results: achieved throughput close to fixed batch 48 but reduced average GPU utilization by 9% due to better packing; end-to-end token cost decreased by 12%. p95 kept under 240ms in steady and burst windows.

E) Snapshotting + cold cache fallback policy:
- Observed that snapshot load time ~7s on node replacement; to avoid 7s penalty we implemented a quick fallback that serves from a smaller quantized variant for the first 10 requests while snapshot loads in background. This limited user-visible tail to ~500ms during node replacements rather than multi-second stalls.

Detailed numbers (selected):
- Demo steady (96 token avg)
  - Baseline p95: 312ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.058
  - Primed + warmup + adaptive batching p95: 172ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.050 (≈13% lower)
- Microburst first spike
  - Baseline p95: 520ms (connection + cold kv)
  - Combined strategy p95: 198ms
- Node replacement window (with snapshot + fallback)
  - Observed user-visible tail: 4.2s -> with fallback reduced to 0.48s (background snapshot still took ~7s but did not block steerable traffic).

Cost model (simplified):
- Inputs: GPU-hour rate (dedicated committed) $6.50/GPU-hour, average tokens per request 96, requests per 1k tokens ~10.4, model compute footprint ~0.00043 GPU-hours per 1k tokens at steady state.
- Baseline monthly projection for 100M tokens: compute $28.0k, storage and egress $3.6k, total ≈ $31.6k.
- With adaptive batching + priming: compute efficiency gains reduce compute by ~12% -> savings ≈ $3.36k/month on 100M tokens.

Recommendations for Cinder Logistics POC demo (short list):
1) Demo config (must-have): KV-cache priming + connection warmup on the dedicated demo pool, adaptive microbatching with target latency 160ms, fallback to quantized variant during snapshot loads.
2) Pre-demo checklist: run the prefix sweep job (100 prefixes) 1 hour before demo start; start warmup script 10 minutes before; verify snapshot loaded on all nodes via /admin/status endpoint.
3) Production rollout: schedule nightly/weekly prefix-sweep jobs that reflect new customer prompts. Include snapshot replication with staggered warmfailover so not all nodes are snapshot-loading simultaneously.
4) Monitoring: add alert on p95 > 250ms over 5m, and on snapshot-load-duration > 10s. Instrument cache hit ratio, connection warmup success rate, and batch rejection rate.

Open questions / next steps (workshop items):
- Which prefixes are safe to synthesize for priming from a privacy and compliance standpoint? (Legal/CS input required.)
- Should we provide an SDK helper for customers to generate warmup traces from their real production logs? (Engineering & DX work item.)
- Validate performance on a lower-memory GPU class (A10s) to reduce unit cost; run a 2-node trial.

Action items (owners):
- Marina: finalize warmup script and publish to repo (due 2029-08-24).
- Ethan: add demo checklist to the Confluence page and link /admin/status checks (due 2029-08-23).
- Priya: confirm data retention/consent for prefix synthesis with CS/legal (due 2029-08-26).

Appendix: quick-run commands and notes:
- Run prefix sweep: python tools/prefix_sweep.py --target-corpus cinder-demo --parallel 40 --duration 6m
- Warmup script (k8s job): kubectl apply -f demos/warmup-job.yaml; job creates 50 streams across pool nodes for 30s
- Snapshot load: admin call POST /admin/snapshot/load?snapshot_id=cinder-aug29-primed

Notes to self: keep the demo pool isolated from traffic shaping experiments; small differences in TLS stack between our test harness and customer Java SDK caused the earlier connection tails (we patched gap by increasing keepalive). Save logs from runs 08/17–08/21 under s3://redwood-poc/cinder/ for deeper forensics.

End of note.
